full_judgment:
2. The suit was instituted on 14.1.1980 for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with the plaintiffs possession in the suit land (0.02 acre) comprising SA Plot No. 1510 under SA Khatian No. 851 and also constituting Holding No. 74 Bangshal Road under Narayangonj Paurashava. 

 3. Briefly stated, the case of the sole plaintiff Abdur Razzak is that the suit property originally belonged to Gobinda Chandra Podder and others, from whom about 40 years ago one Joynal Abedin acquired it. He raised thereon two four chala tin sheds and used to live therein. The property was recorded in his name in SA Khatian. By a kabala executed by Joynal Abedin on 22.10.1965 and registered on 29.11.1965 he sold the property for valuable consideration to the plaintiff. Since then he has been in possession after remodelling the structures. He got his name mutated in Municipal records and paid taxes and also paid rents for the land. The property has also been recorded in his name in RS Khatian after rejection on 21.7.1979 of the defendant's objection. Thereafter the defendants served upon him 2 notices dated 7.9.1979 and 26.9.1979 threatening to dispossess him from the property. 

 4. The Paurashava contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending, inter alia. that the suit land was a part of CS Plot No. 279 (0.40 62 acre) appertaining to Khatian No. 670 belonging to the Paurashava and the plaintiff who got his name mutated in the Paurashava papers by fraudulent means were an unauthorised occupant therein and as such liable to be evicted. Non-maintainability of the suit for want of notice under section 152 of the Paurashava Ordinance was also pleaded in the defence. 

 8. It is not now disputed that SA plot No. 1510 in suit corresponds to southern portion of CS plot No. 298. This 0.02 acre of land with structures thereon constitute Paurashava Holding No. 74. The defendants took the defence that it was a part of CS Plot No. 279 belonging to them. The plaintiff has no claim to CS Plot No. 279 and, on the other hand, the defendants have no claim to CS Plot No. 298, and it has been decided concurrently on the basis of the materials on record including the commissioner's report that the suit holding stands on CS Plot No. 298 and Mr. Fakir Abdul Mannan does not have any submission against this. It will be interesting to note that the 2 notices that is dated 7.9.79 (Ext. 3a) and dated 26.9.79 (Ext. 3b) issued by the Paurashava upon the plaintiff mention only the Holding number. without any settlement plot or Khatian. The former required the plaintiff to appear before the Secretary of the Paurashava at 10:00 AM on 14.9.79 and to show cause why the mutation in his name of the Holding should not be cancelled and the latter actually cancelled the mutation for non-appearance of the plaintiff and also directed him to vacate the property within 7 days, in default of which the Paurashava would take possession thereof by evicting him. It is clear that the Paurashava issued notices under the signatures of its functionaries in official capacity treating the property as belonging to it and the plaintiff as an unauthorised occupant thereof.
